summary.intent: Get PR #467 (feat/tsrs-module-resolution, swapping in the tsrs/oxc module resolver) to a state where all review findings are fixed and resolved so it can merge, independent of the 0.11.0 release PR #396.
summary.outcome: Three blocking findings were fixed in 7c9e384b and resolved after a source check. A fourth finding then showed that the resolution fingerprint became a constant, which exposed a wrong root-cause diagnosis. The worker was sent a broader task: inventory all resolution-keyed caches, write a cross-run matrix test, and hash the effective inputs. #467 stays out of the release.

repo: Anything that outlives a run and is keyed on resolver inputs must change with them: the persisted dependency index, in-memory resolvers, watch invalidation, and kept-answer fingerprints. The old resolver's options hash covered all of this implicitly.

The old resolution_fingerprint hashed the full resolver options, including customConditions inherited through extends. The new one hashes a constant, the root tsconfig path and mtime, and the build, so edits to an extended config don't invalidate the cache.
The old fingerprint probably only tracked the root tsconfig's mtime, so extended-config `paths` edits may never have invalidated the cache even on main. This is unverified.
Fixtures never exercised the tsrs/oxc contract boundaries: symlink path identity, importer mode (.cts), cwd base for relative tsconfig, and project references.
The identity diff is a single-run check and cannot catch cross-run stale-cache bugs.

code.finding: resolve_path canonicalizes its result before it is used as a declaration key, which fixes imports through relative symlinks.
A .cts importer resolves with the require condition first and falls back to import. The resolution scope is part of the cache key.
The configured tsconfig path is made absolute against the working directory before parsing (also at lines 119 and 149).
The fingerprint constant leaves the dependency-index fingerprint unchanged when extended-config customConditions change.
read_index accepts cached package answers when the fingerprint matches, so a stale fingerprint reuses old data.
find_export_in returns old declaration targets from the cached index, producing stale props on later runs.

workflow: Shell variables holding CLI flags break in zsh because they are not word-split, so pass flags explicitly (the `entire trail finding resolve` calls failed this way and were retried).
Read the fix in source on the remote branch before resolving findings, rather than trusting a subagent hand-back.
Before calling a root cause settled, ask what state outlives a run and is keyed on the replaced component's inputs.

For cache and fingerprint changes, write the cross-run test first: run 1 writes the cache, one input is perturbed, and run 2 must equal a cold run. Also run it against main's binary to expose pre-existing holes.
A control test showing that clearing the cache makes an edit visible does not prove the real watch-invalidation test would fail if invalidation were removed.

friction: Three review findings, then a fourth in the same class, showed the earlier 'three boundaries' root cause was too narrow. The user was frustrated.
The identity diff gate and fixture suite could not detect cross-run staleness, so the bug reached review.
The shell-variable flag expansion failure forced a retry of the finding resolutions.
The subagent's hand-back claimed a settled root cause that later proved incomplete.
open_items: The worker must inventory every resolution-keyed cache, fingerprint, and invalidation rule and put the inventory in the PR body.
Write and pass the cross-run matrix test: extended customConditions, extended paths/baseUrl, referenced project options, dependency exports, and symlink target.
Fix the fingerprint to hash the effective options after extends, plus path, mtime, and length of every config in the chain and references, not a constant.
Verify on main's binary whether extended-config `paths` edits already failed to invalidate the cache.
Still not run: gate-measure, watch RSS, wall time, and other crates. The stale-resolver watch check is a control, not an inversion of the real test.
Check the findings list again once CI on the new head finishes (13 passing, 6 pending at last check).
Release PR #396 has an unverified stripped Linux build. #467 should follow #396 and not ship in 0.11.0.
